samples.summary: Text-box `getSelectionStyle()` changed from raw to effective style; the shared colour/highlight swatches (an out-of-diff consumer, reached from slides via delegation) now display a named-style default as the caret's colour
samples.evidence: `packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:980` now returns `{ ...caretStyle(true), ...staged }` — named-style inline defaults layered in — where it previously returned the raw `inline.style`. `packages/slides/src/view/editor/text-box-editor.ts:599` delegates straight through, and `packages/frontend/src/components/text-formatting/text-format-group.tsx:90` (`const selectionStyle = editor?.getSelectionStyle();`) feeds the text-colour / highlight swatch's current value. For a slides text box whose block is a heading, built-in `heading-6` supplies `color: '#666666'`, so the swatch now renders that as the run's colour even though no run carries it; previously it was `undefined` and the component fell back to its own default. The four B/I/U/S toggles in the same file were migrated to the range summary, but the swatch reads were deliberately left on the caret read whose meaning changed underneath them.

samples.summary: The shared `TextFormattingEditor.getSelectionStyle()` contract is now implemented with two different meanings by its two implementers, and its doc comment still describes only the old one
samples.evidence: `types.ts:22` documents `getSelectionStyle(): Partial<InlineStyle>` as "the inline style at the current cursor/selection anchor". After this change the docs full editor (`packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:995`, `caretInlineStyle(doc, cursor.position, /* withStyleDefaults */ false)` by default) still returns the RAW run style, while the docs/slides text-box editor (`packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:980`) returns the EFFECTIVE style with named-style defaults merged. Any shared component written against this interface — `TextFormatGroup`, `TextStyleGroup`, the slides text-edit section — now gets surface-dependent semantics from one method. The fix belongs either on `types.ts` (state which layer callers get) or on `editor.ts` so both sides agree.

samples.summary: Slides' `SlidesTextBoxEditor.getSelectionStyle` declaration and the docs `TextBoxEditorAPI` declaration still document/imply the old raw-style contract after the behaviour change
samples.evidence: `packages/slides/src/view/editor/text-box-editor.ts:234-239` introduces the block as "Delegated straight through to the underlying docs TextBoxEditorAPI so shared text-formatting toolbar components can drive the slides text-box editor via the same `TextFormattingEditor` interface as the docs editor" — an equivalence that no longer holds, since the docs full editor's `getSelectionStyle` stays raw and the text-box one is now effective. `packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:224` likewise declares the method with no note that its result now includes named-style defaults, while the sibling `getRangeStyleSummary` declaration below it is fully documented.

samples.summary: The slim header/footer toolbar's colour and highlight swatches still read the caret style while its B/I/U toggles were switched to the range summary — the same caret/range disagreement the change is fixing, left on the adjacent lines
samples.evidence: `docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:422` keeps `const slimSelectionStyle = editor?.getSelectionStyle();` and lines 485 and 507 use it for `color={slimSelectionStyle?.color ...}` / `slimSelectionStyle?.backgroundColor`. With a backward (right-to-left) selection the caret sits at the range's start, so — by the very premise this change documents and pins in `packages/docs/test/view/backward-selection-toggle.test.ts` — those swatches display the colour of the run PRECEDING the selection while the Bold/Italic/Underline buttons beside them now describe the selection itself. `getRangeStyleSummary()` already returns `color` / `backgroundColor` (`packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2648` KEYS list), so the same summary the toggles use could drive them.

samples.summary: `Doc.applyInlineStyle` silently becomes a no-op for a range whose endpoint does not resolve to a context block, and none of its three callers can detect that nothing was written
samples.evidence: `range-slices.ts:196-198` returns early when `doc.getBlockIndex()` yields -1 for either normalized endpoint (an endpoint inside a nested table, or parentage stale since the last layout). The write callers — `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1031`, `packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:2935`, `packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:822` — all call `doc.applyInlineStyle(...)` for its side effect only (it returns `void`), then unconditionally `docStore.snapshot()`/`saveSnapshot()` beforehand and `render()` after. The result is an undo entry recorded for a write that never happened and no user-visible feedback; `packages/docs/test/model/table.test.ts` (new nested-table case) pins the no-op as intended, so this is about the callers' inability to observe it rather than the traversal itself.

finding.summary: New single write path `applyStyleToSelection` marks dirty with a context-relative index against the body block array — wrong block (or a crash) when editing a header/footer
finding.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:2935-2952 — `startIdx/endIdx` come from `this.doc.getBlockIndex()`, which resolves against `Doc.getContextBlocks()` (document.ts:211-212, header/footer aware), but line 2951 dereferences `this.doc.document.blocks[i].id` (body only). While editing a header/footer, a cross-block style write marks an unrelated body block dirty and, when the header has more blocks than the body (e.g. header index 2, body length 1), `this.doc.document.blocks[i]` is `undefined` and `.id` throws. The diff consolidates the B/I/U/S toggles, clear formatting (Cmd+\) and the format painter apply into this one function and documents it as "a body range marks the span", so all three keyboard commands now share the mismatch. The code itself is relocated from the old `toggleStyle`/`clearFormatting`, so the defect predates the diff, but the diff makes it the single write path for every keyboard style command.

verdict.reason: The finding asserts that `applyStyleToSelection` marks dirty using `startIdx/endIdx` from `this.doc.getBlockIndex()` fed into `this.doc.document.blocks[i].id`. That code is not present. `applyStyleToSelection` (text-editor.ts:2921-2940) contains no index arithmetic: the cell-rectangle branch marks `range.tableCellRange.blockId`, and the general branch marks ids from `dirtyBlockIdsForRange(this.doc, range)` (line 2938). The cited lines 2942-2951 are `getStyleAtCursor()`, which just returns `caretInlineStyle(...)`. The dirty-marking helper (range-slices.ts:109-115) derives ids from `visitRangeSlices`, whose top-level cross-block walk indexes `doc.getContextBlocks()` — the same header/footer-aware array `getBlockIndex` resolves against (document.ts:98-102, 211-213) — and guards both `anchorIdx/focusIdx < 0` (line 198) and a missing `block` (line 209). So neither the wrong-block nor the undefined-dereference outcome can occur on this path. A structurally similar body-array pattern does exist at text-editor.ts:2273-2279 (`forEachBlockInSelection`, used by indent/outdent), editor.ts:1344-1348 and text-box-editor.ts:797-803, but those are different functions on non-style paths and are not what this finding describes; the finding's claim is specifically that the consolidated keyboard-style write path carries the mismatch, and it does not.

finding.summary: `applyStyleImpl`'s dirty-marking still uses the body-only `layout.blockParentMap` and `doc.document.blocks[i]`, while the reads it now agrees with moved to the merged `doc.blockParentMap`
finding.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1032-1048 (and the identical copy at 2965-2982 in `insertLink`): the reads in this diff were deliberately switched to `doc.blockParentMap` (the header+footer+body merged map built at editor.ts:1291-1298) because `layout.blockParentMap` cannot resolve a header/footer table cell. The write's dirty-marking here was not: it still asks `layout.blockParentMap`, so for a caret/range inside a *header or footer* table cell both lookups miss, execution falls to `doc.getBlockIndex()` (header-context indices) and then indexes `doc.document.blocks[i]` (body), marking the wrong block dirty or dereferencing `undefined.id`. The style is written correctly by the newly shared traversal but the affected region can render stale.

verdict.reason: The described code is not present. `applyStyleImpl` at packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1031-1036 marks dirty via `for (const id of dirtyBlockIdsForRange(doc, range)) markDirty(id)` — no `layout.blockParentMap` lookup, no `getBlockIndex`, no `doc.document.blocks[i]`. `insertLink`'s range path at editor.ts:2948-2950 uses the identical shared call (the cited 2965-2982 is the caret-inside-existing-link branch, not a duplicated range dirty-marking block). The shared helper `dirtyBlockIdsForRange` (model/range-slices.ts:109-115) resolves parents through `topLevelBlockId` (range-slices.ts:80-92), which reads the merged `doc.blockParentMap` — the same map the reads use — and its cross-block walk (range-slices.ts:196-208) pairs `doc.getBlockIndex()` with `doc.getContextBlocks()`, the region-correct array, never `doc.document.blocks`. `doc.blockParentMap` is the merged header+footer+body map set at editor.ts:1276-1283, so a header/footer table cell resolves in the write path too. Grepping the whole package for `document.blocks[` / `getBlockIndex` / `layout.blockParentMap` found no site matching the described mechanism in these two functions; other `layout.blockParentMap` uses (e.g. editor.ts:1325-1326, 1372, 2970, 3007) are different code paths and none index the body block array.
